title: SLO Failure-Mode Mapping and Capacity Safety-Net Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========
This playbook describes a structured mapping between observable failure modes, their direct impact on SLOs and error budgets, and the pre-authorized capacity safety-net responses that oncall and SRE engineers should execute. The goal is to enable fast, consistent decisions that balance reliability, cost, and customer impact during both transient and sustained degradation events.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API + dedicated pools).
- Covers SLO classes: Latency P95/P99, Availability (request success rate), and Staleness (model version drift).
- Integrates with: telemetry (Prometheus/Tempo), traffic control (traffic-router), autoscaler, and capacity-shimming tooling (burst-absorber).

Why this matters
-----------------
When an incident begins, the observed metric is rarely the direct SLO. Delay in mapping symptoms to SLO impact leads to overreaction (expensive capacity) or underreaction (missed SLAs). This playbook codifies failure-mode -> SLO -> action mappings and pre-authorized budget/capacity escalations so responders can act immediately.

Key concepts and glossary
-------------------------
- Failure mode: a distinct observable class (e.g., KV-cache-thrashing, GC-saturation-on-inference-nodes, model-kernel-fallback).
- Safety-net capacity: a reserved pool or fast-burst allocation used only for incident mitigation (not routine autoscale).
- Error budget action tier: pre-agreed actions tied to remaining error budget (See Error Budget Actions table).
- SLO impact vector: how a failure mode affects SLOs (latency tail, availability, transient 5xx spike).

High-level decision flow (summary)
--------------------------------
1) Detect: alert fires with evidence (telemetry + synthetic).
2) Triage: map alert -> failure mode (use table below).
3) Estimate: project SLO hit if current pattern persists for 30m / 3h.
4) Act: run pre-authorized mitigation (safety-net allocation, traffic shaping, model fallback).
5) Observe: verify SLO trajectory and reduce actions if no improvement.
6) Post-incident: run incident review using "Failure-Mode RCA" template.

Failure-mode mapping table (core)
--------------------------------
| Failure mode identifier | Primary observables | SLO impact vector | Immediate mitigation | Ownership | Escalation threshold |
|-------------------------|---------------------|-------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| kv-cache-thrashing | KV miss rate > 20% and CPU steal on cache-proxy | Latency P99 spike, token cost increase | WARMER: trigger cache prewarm, reduce batch size by 25%, enable short-lived safety-net pool (burst-absorber:cache) | infra-sre | 10m sustained
| gpu-scheduling-starvation | Pending GPU pods > 5% of pool and queue backlog grows | Availability for dedicated customers, requests queued | Drain low-priority pools, allocate safety-net GPU nodes (safety-net:gpu-fairshare), enable routing to secondary region | runtime-oncall | 5m sustained or 50% error budget consumed
| kernel-fallbacks (FP16->FP32) | Increased per-token latency + kernel fallback logs | Latency P95/P99 regression | Switch to a compatible quantization profile, enable micro-restarts of affected worker subset | serving-runtime | 15m sustained
| control-plane-backpressure | Control-plane API errors 5xx > 1% | Availability for control-plane operations (deploys, rollouts) | Limit new rollouts, activate control-plane read-only mode, use pre-approved emergency maintenance window | infra-sre + platform | immediate for >1% 10m
| model-version-staleness | Model version mismatch count > 0.5% of requests | Output correctness SLO (quality) | Failover to pinned model version, pause new model onboards | model-onboarding | 30m sustained or first detection in production

Error budget action tiers
------------------------
- Tier 0 (green): error budget > 75% — standard autoscale; no mitigation required.
- Tier 1 (amber): error budget 50–75% — proactive mitigations allowed: select non-disruptive traffic shaping, temporary cache warmers.
- Tier 2 (red): error budget 25–50% — safety-net capacity allocation allowed, temporary downscaling of non-critical tenants.
- Tier 3 (critical): error budget < 25% — emergency actions: global routing changes, customer rate-limiting, rollbacks.

Pre-authorized capacity safety-net policies
-----------------------------------------
- Safety-net pools are tagged and billed to a central "resilience" budget. Use is audited and requires follow-up postmortem with cost attribution.
- Allocation rules:
  - Burst-absorber:cache — up to 20% extra CPU capacity for caching tier for up to 60 minutes per incident.
  - Safety-net:gpu-fairshare — hot-standby GPUs (max 8 nodes per region) usable for 2 hours.
  - Safety-net:dedicated-burst — reserve equivalent of one medium dedicated pool for emergency customer routing (max once per 24 hours per org).
- Guardrails:
  - Any allocation that uses safety-net:gpu-fairshare requires an incident lead approval (or automatic if error budget < 25%).
  - Automated throttle will reduce safety-net spending if projected cost > $X (internal budget tag).

Operational runbook: triage checklist (quick)
-------------------------------------------
1) Confirm alert validity: check Prometheus query, synthetic check, and traces (Tempo).
   - Example PromQL for P99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
2) Identify failure mode using recent logs and metrics (use failure-mode mapping table).
3) Compute projected SLO impact: assume current rate for 30 minutes; calculate error budget consumption. Use quick calculator script: scripts/estimate_error_budget.sh --service <svc> --window 30m
4) Select mitigation from mapping table and execute pre-authorized action. Record action in incident timeline.
5) After 10 minutes, reassess. If no improvement, escalate to next tier and allocate safety-net capacity.

Operational runbook: mitigation recipes (examples)
-------------------------------------------------
- Cache prewarm and batch tuning
  1. Trigger cache prewarm job: kubectl -n infra run cache-prewarm --image=registry/redwood/cache-prewarm:stable -- /prewarm --service <svc> --prefixes 100
  2. Reduce batch size: update configmap svc-batching -> BATCH_SIZE = floor(BATCH_SIZE * 0.75) and roll polling config to 10s.
- Safety-net GPU allocation (fast path)
  1. Run: gcloud compute instances create-from-template safety-net-gpu-template --zone=<zone> --labels=incident=<id>
  2. Add instances to autoscaler pool: scripts/attach_gpu_to_pool.sh --pool inference-dedicated --instance-group <ig>
  3. Notify router: curl -X POST $ROUTER_API/override -d '{"pool":"safety-net:gpu-fairshare","duration":"120m"}'
- Model fallback
  1. Pin to previous model version: curl -X POST $CONFIG_API/models/<model>/pin -d '{"version":"v123"}'
  2. Pause model promotion jobs in CI: ci pause-job projects/model-promote --model <model>

Monitoring and observability guidance
------------------------------------
- Synthetic tail-slo probes: run synthetic trace for representative token lengths every 2 minutes for P95 and P99 latency. Alert if synthetic P99 > target by 30%.
- Dashboard required widgets for each serviced SLO: latency histogram, error-rate time-series, queue length, cache hit ratio, GPUS in use, backlog length.
- Tracing correlation: ensure traces include routing decision and kernel-selection tags to speed root cause mapping.

Incident review standards (failure-mode RCA)
--------------------------------------------
Post-incident writeup must include:
1) Executive summary and customer impact (1 paragraph).
2) Timeline with actions and timestamps (ISO8601).
3) Failure-mode identification and reasoning: which failure mode(s) were primary vs secondary.
4) SLO/error-budget impact with graphs and numerical estimates.
5) Safety-net usage: what was allocated, duration, and cost estimate.
6) Root cause analysis and recommended remediation (short-term + long-term).
7) Action owner(s), deadlines, and verification tests.

Template checklist for reviewers
-------------------------------
- Did the responders map the observables to a documented failure mode?
- Were pre-authorized mitigations used before ad-hoc changes?
- Was safety-net capacity used appropriately and recorded?
- Are remediation tasks actionable and timeboxed?
- Is there a test to validate the fix?

Automation and tooling integrations
---------------------------------
- Telemetry playbooks: use alert-runbook links that include the failure-mode mapping table for one-click remediation suggestions in the alert UI.
- Error budget calculator: a small lambda service accepts service, window, and projects expected error budget consumption; integrate this into pager messages.
- Safety-net audit: every safety-net allocation triggers a GitHub issue template populated by automation that the incident lead must complete.

Ownership matrix and SLAs for actions
------------------------------------
- Oncall responder: initial detection and triage (first 15m).
- Runtime/Serving owner: mitigation of kernel/fallbacks and model fallbacks (action within 30m).
- Infra-SRE: capacity allocations and control-plane actions (action within 15m for capacity and immediate for control-plane).
- Postmortem owner: incident lead assigned; ensure RCA published within 7 business days.

Runbook maintenance and cadence
------------------------------
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by Eng-SRE reliability guild.
- After any safety-net allocation, update the playbook if any step required an ad-hoc workaround.
- Track labels: add label 'safety-net-used' to incident tickets to support quarterly audits.

Appendix A — quick reference cheatsheet (for oncall)
---------------------------------------------------
- If P99 latency > SLO by 50% for 10m: check cache hit ratio -> if < 80% trigger cache prewarm, reduce batch size, and enable flash pool.
- If 5xx rate > 1% and queue backlog rising: allocate safety-net:gpu-fairshare and divert non-critical tenants.
- If model quality alerts trigger: pin model and stop promotions. Notify ML-onboarding immediately.

Appendix B — example PromQL alerts
-----------------------------------
- High P99 latency:
  alert: ServiceHighP99
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 1.5 * scalar(target_p99_seconds)
  for: 10m
- Growing GPU backlog:
  alert: GPUBacklogGrowing
  expr: max(rate(pending_pod_count[5m])) by (region) > 0.05 * scalar(total_gpu_pods)
  for: 5m

Contact and escalation list
---------------------------
- Primary oncall: see pager rota in Confluence /oncall (links embedded in alert)
- Infra-SRE lead: ravi.menon@redwood.local
- Serving runtime lead: leah.kim@redwood.local
- Pager escalation: page All-SRE if incident enters Tier 3 or error budget < 25%

End of document
